summary:
KeratoClean: Turning Tannery Waste into Cleaner Water Through Earth Observation.
KeratoClean is an eco-friendly solution that transforms discarded tannery hair into a low-cost bio-adsorbent for wastewater treatment. Through heat treatment and chemical activation, tannery hair is converted into a porous material with the potential to remove pollutants such as dyes, chromium, and suspended particles from industrial wastewater.
To extend its environmental impact, KeratoClean integrates NASA's Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) IMERG satellite data with QGIS-based spatial analysis. We explore monthly, seasonal, and annual precipitation variations to identify geographical patterns, measure rainfall trends, and assess their statistical significance.
Since precipitation influences surface runoff, water availability, and potential pollutant movement, understanding its changing patterns can provide valuable environmental context for industrial pollution management. By comparing rainfall patterns with tannery locations and available environmental information, we aim to identify areas that may require further pollution monitoring.
KeratoClean connects circular waste management, sustainable wastewater treatment, and Earth observation technology. It supports SDG 6 , SDG 9 , and SDG 12 .
Our vision is to transform industrial waste into an opportunity for cleaner water while using NASA Earth science data to support a more sustainable future.
details:
KeratoClean: Sustainable Wastewater Treatment

KeratoClean transforms hazardous tannery hair waste into an affordable bio-adsorbent through heat treatment and phosphoric acid activation. Using 50g of adsorbent per 10L of wastewater, it targets the removal of turbidity (85–90%), dyes (80–85%), and chromium (70–80%).

Benefits & Impact: At an estimated cost of 150 BDT/kg, KeratoClean offers a low-cost alternative to commercial activated carbon while promoting waste recycling and cleaner water. It supports SDGs 6, 9, and 12, with potential applications in Bangladesh's tannery and textile industries.

Tools & Data: NASA GPM IMERG precipitation data, QGIS, Excel, CapCut, and laboratory equipment.

Creativity & Innovation: KeratoClean combines waste-to-resource innovation with NASA Earth-observation data to identify rainfall-driven pollution patterns and support strategic filtration deployment.

Key Considerations: Production cost, scalability, raw material availability, market adoption, treatment efficiency, and safe disposal of used adsorbents.
